churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, configuration and formatting are each centralized with types at the boundaries, so framework/data changes touch few files; the duplicated route table, triple scroll logic and router-outlet CSS selectors are the friction points.

findings.issue: fetch(url) is never given an AbortSignal, and every resource loader destructures only {params} (e.g. app/src/app/pages/pokemon/pokemon-page.ts:45). Angular's resource aborts the loader when params change or the component is destroyed, but the underlying network requests keep running; a hung API also leaves a page loading forever.
findings.suggestion: Accept an optional AbortSignal in PokeApi.get and pass it to fetch ({signal}); thread loader({params, abortSignal}) through, optionally combining with AbortSignal.timeout.

findings.issue: The dependent moves resource reads this.data.value() inside params() — the exact pattern the Angular v22 resource guide calls out ('reads value() directly without status propagation'); v22 added chain() for this, which mirrors loading/error states and avoids the manual hasValue()/isLoading() gymnastics in the template.
findings.suggestion: Use params: ({chain}) => { const view = chain(this.data); return view && this.selectedGame() ? {pokemon: view.pokemon, game: this.selectedGame()!.name} : undefined; } (source: angular.dev/guide/signals/resource, 'Chaining resources').

findings.issue: Route knowledge is duplicated: DETAIL_ROUTES/STATIC_ROUTES restate the URL patterns of app/src/app/app.routes.ts, and the 404 HEAD-probe couples the static server to PokeAPI resource names. Adding or renaming a route requires touching both files, and a divergence silently breaks either 404 status or the served page.
findings.suggestion: Export the route patterns from one shared manifest consumed by both app.routes.ts and the server, or drop the server-side 404 check entirely (the spec makes 404 optional) and let the app's not-found page handle it.

findings.issue: An effect sets searchText from the q input — signal-to-signal state propagation inside an effect, which the Angular guidance explicitly discourages, plus manual lastSearchSent bookkeeping to avoid feedback loops.
findings.suggestion: Use linkedSignal(() => this.q() ?? '') as the search box state; it is the current API for writable state linked to a source and eliminates the effect and the lastSent tracking.

findings.issue: Scroll-to-top is hand-rolled here and again in home.ts:66-69 and pokemon-page.ts:63-67; the router already provides withInMemoryScrolling({scrollPositionRestoration: 'enabled'}) for the navigation case, so this is copy-pasted behavior the framework covers (only the post-load #fragment jump genuinely needs custom code).
findings.suggestion: Enable withInMemoryScrolling in provideRouter for the navigation scroll reset, keeping the custom after-render fragment jump as the single exception.

findings.issue: Global CSS selects the router-outlet element (.site-main > :not(router-outlet)) and component-internal classes (app-load-state, app-not-found) to lay out routed pages, coupling the stylesheet to how the router renders views.
findings.suggestion: Give routed components a wrapper element or host class (e.g. host: {class: 'page'}) and target that instead of router-outlet internals.

findings.issue: @angular/forms is a runtime dependency but is never imported anywhere in app/src (grep: 0 matches), and the app deliberately uses plain native elements with manual bindings.

Uses afterNextRender with an explicit injector plus the global document for the #moves jump; the current guidance for signal-driven DOM side effects is afterRenderEffect (which also removes the need for inject(Injector)), and inject(DOCUMENT) is used elsewhere (api-config.ts) but not here.
findings.suggestion: Replace the effect + afterNextRender pair with afterRenderEffect({write: ...}) and inject(DOCUMENT) for consistency; afterNextRender is still supported, so this is a modernization, not a fix.

summary: This is a thoroughly current Angular 22 codebase: resource()-based data loading, signal inputs from the router, the new @Service() decorator, zoneless/OnPush defaults taken for granted, zero-dependency platform-first implementation. The main forward-looking gaps are the two patterns the v22 resource docs prescribe and this code skips — abortSignal plumbed into fetch and chain() for the dependent moves resource — plus a duplicated route table in the static server and some hand-rolled scroll/CSS reaching into router internals. It would ride an Angular upgrade with very little churn.

apis.replacement: v22 resource chaining; preferred over reading data.value() in params() per angular.dev/guide/signals/resource
preferred over effect+set for search-box state synced from the URL input
afterRenderEffect() is the current recommendation for signal-driven DOM side effects
